newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean court overturns Davila's tax conviction.
newsitem.headline: Chilean court overturns Davila's tax conviction.

text.p: A Chilean appeals court has overturned former Codelco futures trader Juan Pablo Davila's conviction for tax evasion and revoked his three year jail sentence and a monetary fine, judicial sources said.

Investigating judge Jose Benquis, who convicted Davila two months ago, had fined the ex-trader 133 million pesos, or $324,000, in the first conviction from a futures trading scandal which cost Chile $175 million in 1993.
In its ruling the court said that the money Davila failed to declare to the tax authorities "could present legal and criminal questions which do not allow such an early jail sentence."
Davila, once Codelco's top futures operator, was accused of failing to declare 220 million pesos, or around half $500,000, on his income tax forms in 1993.
The ex-trader, who still faces a slew of other fraud charges, was released from jail on bail in early August to undergo cancer treatment.
The scandal forced Codelco's president to resign and shocked the world's metal markets.
Davila originally said the losses were due to trading errors which he tried to cover in risky speculative deals, but he was later charged with fraud and put under preventative arrest.

Codelco has started court cases in London against two brokers, Sogemin Metals Limited and Metallgesellschaft, accusing them of paying secret commissions to Davila who was fired as soon as the losses were uncovered.
